releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- 1727442: fix(ai): process only the first approval response per tool call, so repeated or conflicting responses in the final tool message no longer execute a tool twice or both execute and deny it
- 0a5d0e7: Fix `toolChoice: 'none'` by forwarding it to the Hugging Face Responses API and rejecting tool calls before local execution in `generateText`, `streamText`, and `WorkflowAgent`. Streamed tool parts are withheld so client-side tools cannot act on them, and `repairToolCall` and `experimental_refineToolInput` are not invoked for rejected tool calls.
- 10026d1: Add the `interrupted` finish reason for provider streams that end without a completion signal. Preserve partial output without introducing an error solely for interruption, and stop tool execution, agent continuation, and automatic UI follow-ups for interrupted responses, including late tool results and approvals. Provider detection and emission will be added separately.

  **Compatibility notice:** Adding `interrupted` to the public finish-reason types can break type checking after upgrading, even though this is a patch release. Exhaustive switches (for example, using an `assertNever` fallback) and mappings such as `Record<FinishReason, string>` must handle the new value. Update any custom validation or application logic that assumes the existing set of finish reasons is exhaustive.

  When providers begin emitting `interrupted`, a stream ending without a completion signal will preserve partial output and report this finish reason without emitting an error solely for the interruption. Applications that need to detect incomplete responses should check `finishReason === 'interrupted'` as well as their existing error handling.

> **Action required**

> - fix(vk)!: correct profile phone number type ([#11849](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11849))
>
>   VK profile callbacks now accept phone numbers as strings. Profile mappings must treat `user.phone` as a string instead of a number.
> - If you use Naver profile mappings, update them to handle omitted personal fields and supply an email when Naver does not share one. ([#11858](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11858))
> - If you use Kakao profile mappings, update them to handle a missing `kakao_account`. ([#11857](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11857))

> - fix(linkedin)!: correct profile locale type ([#11844](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11844))
>
>   LinkedIn profile callbacks now accept locale language tags such as `en-US`. Profile mappings must read `locale` as a string instead of a country/language object.
> - If your Google profile mappings rely on ID token claims such as email verification, update them to handle claims that are now optional. ([#11847](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11847))
> - fix(huggingface)!: align organization profile types ([#11845](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11845))
>
>   Hugging Face profile mappings must iterate over organization arrays and can read optional plan and security restrictions. Organization roles are strings; use `securityRestrictions` instead of the deprecated SSO and MFA flags.
> - If you use `mapProfileToUser` with Polar, update it to read the scoped, nullable userinfo claims instead of the previous user profile fields. ([#11840](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11840))
> - If you use custom Kick profile mappings or `getUserInfo` callbacks, update them to treat `KickProfile.user_id` as a number instead of a string. ([#11841](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11841))

releases.name: v1.0.0-rc.5
releases.body:
# ORM


- [BREAKING] Fixed `postgres-js` transparent parsers set by `drizzle()` constructors breaking driver's own serializers for `timestamptz`, `timestamp`, `date`, `time`, `json`, `jsonb` types (fixes #3171, #4426, #5789)  paramsInErrors
 :exclamation: Any existing workarounds with manual `JSON.stringify(jsonValue)` in raw sql or raw driver calls must be removed to prevent double stringification of JSON params; For array-type JSON params in `sql` use `sql.param(jsonArrayValue)` to avoid it being parsed as value list instead of param.    
- [BREAKING] Restricted `undefined` value passed to fields in relational queries' `where` - now throws an error upon encountering `undefined` in filters, added `EmptyFilter` symbol (`import { EmptyFilter } from 'drizzle-orm/relations'`) that can be used as an explicit replacement of `undefined` where possibly absent filter is desired by design rather than possible bug (fixes #5636)  
  Example: 
  ```typescript
    db.query.users.findMany({ where: { isActive: params.isActive ?? EmptyFilter } })
  ```
- [BREAKING] Relation filters without conditions (`{}`, or containing only empty conditions) are now skipped like any other empty filter instead of generating `exists (...)` check of relation's presence - use `true` to filter by relation's presence, `false` - by its absence  
  Example:
  ```typescript
    // Previously: `where exists (select * from "posts" ...)`, now: no filter
    db.query.users.findMany({ where: { posts: {} } })
    // Users with at least one post
    db.query.users.findMany({ where: { posts: true } })
  ```
- [BREAKING] Updated `postgres` codecs: now generic codecs contain only in-json codecs (mirroring `mysql`), contents of drivers' codecs remain unchanged
- [BREAKING] Switched `pg` `bytea` in-json codecs from `encode(..., 'base64')` casts to decoding `to_json`'s native hex output
- [BREAKING] Made nested select join nullification consider `SQL` field data during nullification
- [BREAKING] Fixed `sqlite` ignoring `.$defaultFn(...)` on insert when `.default(...)` is present
- [BREAKING] Untied `bun-sql/mysql`, `mysql2`, `singlestore` column mapping from connection config, removed forced `bigint` params on their respective configs, replaced with more stable `cast` codecs
- [BREAKING] Reworked `cockroach` column builders to mirror `pg` - now both have same `.array('[][]...')` syntax
- [BREAKING] Moved `View` exports from `drizzle-orm/sql/sql` to `drizzle-orm/view`
- [BREAKING] `getTableUniqueName` no longer prefixes aliased views or tables with their `schema`
- [BREAKING] `getTableUniqueName` no longer sets `public.` prefix for entities without `schema`
- [BREAKING] Updated `View` class: switched to `Table`-like object config for type template, typed `schema` property
- [BREAKING] Updated `withReplicas` (indirectly fixes #4185): 
  - Now every query goes to primary db by default
  - To query replica, explicitly call `db.$replica`
- [BREAKING] Added `withCastCodecs = false` switch to `getSQL()`, `withCastCodecs = true` switch to `toSQL()` of non-relational query builders - now `db.select(...).from(...).getSQL()` emits query without cast codecs by default  
- [BREAKING] Reworked `sqlite-proxy`: 
  - Added `rowMode: 'array' | 'object'` switch for `'all' | 'get'` execute methods
  - Dropped `{ rows: Result[] }` callback result wrapping - now expected direct return of expected data
  - Replaced `callback`, `batchCallback` with `SqliteProxyExecutors` object - must provide `run`, `all`, `get` handlers & optional `batch` handler
  - Dropped `values` execute method due to it being duplicate of array-mode `all`
  - Added `TRunResult` type inferrence based on return type of `run` executor, updated `SqliteRemoteDatabase` template with `TRunResult` argument
  - Added per-item `rowMode: 'array' | 'object'` to `batch`, `batch` is expected to mirror executors' return types per query
- [BREAKING] Fixed runtime-type expected result mismatch for `get` (`data | undefined` in runtime, `data[]` in types) (fixes #5461, #3394)
- [BREAKING] Fixed `sqlite` `db.get(sql)` return type lacking `| undefined` for queries without returned rows
- [BREAKING] Omitted query `params` from `DrizzleQueryError` by default, added `paramsInErrors` option to `drizzle` constructor to enable query `params` in `DrizzleQueryError` (fixes #5939)  
  Example:
  ```typescript
  const db = drizzle({
    connection: 'postgres://...',
    paramsInErrors: true 
  })
  ```
- [BREAKING] For `mysql`, `postgres`, `cockroach`, `mssql` set RQBv2 to new query build strategy to fix slow query plans (fixes #5245)  
  Can be opted out of per query via `strategy` switch: `db.query.findMany({ strategy: 'basic' })`
  When used, may break direct references to relations in raw SQL syntax `where`, `orderBy`:
  ```typescript
  // posts with the most comments first
  db.query.posts.findMany({
	with: { author: true, comments: true },
	orderBy: (t, { sql }) => sql`json_array_length("comments"."r") desc, ${t.id}`, // "comments" becomes unreachable due to query nesting
	limit: 2,
  });
  
  // posts of verified authors
  db.query.posts.findMany({
	with: { author: true },
	where: { RAW: (t, { sql }) => sql`("author"."r"->>'verified')::boolean` }, // "author" becomes unreachable due to query nesting
  });
  ```
- [BREAKING] Moved `StringChunk`, `commonStringChunks` exports from `drizzle-orm/sql/sql` to `drizzle-orm/sql/common-chunks` (still exported from `drizzle-orm/sql`)
- [BREAKING] Switched RQBv2 build functions to chunk collection: each accepts optional trailing `collectTo: SQLChunk[]` array to push chunks to and returns chunk arrays instead of `SQL`  
  :exclamation: Chunk arrays embedded into `sql` directly are rendered as value lists - wrap them in `new SQL(chunks)` to use them as query parts  
  - `relationsFilterToSQL(...).sql`: `SQL | undefined` -> `SQLChunk[] | undefined`, added `collectTo` parameter
  - `relationsOrderToSQL(...)`: `SQL | undefined` -> `SQLChunk[] | undefined`, added `collectTo` parameter
  - `relationsOrderEntriesToSQL(...)`: replaced `parts: SQL[]` parameter with `collectTo: SQLChunk[]`, `start?: number`; `RelationsOrderSource`'s `from`, `filters` are now `SQLChunk[]`, `SQLChunk[][]`
  - `relationExtrasToSQL(...).sql`: `SQL | undefined` -> `SQLChunk[] | undefined`, added `collectTo` parameter
  - `relationToSQL(...)`: `{ filter?: SQL; joinCondition?: SQL }` -> `{ filter: SQLChunk[]; joinCondition?: SQLChunk[] }`, added `filterTo`, `joinConditionTo` parameters
  - `getTableAsAliasSQL(...)`: `SQL` -> `SQLChunk[]`, added `collectTo` parameter
- [BREAKING] Relational queries are now cached by caches with `all` strategy (`global: true`), opt out per query via `withCache: false`
- [BREAKING] Replaced `DBQueryConfigWithComment` type with `DBQueryConfigRoot` - config of root relational query containing all root-only options (`strategy`, `comment`, `withCache`); dialects' relational query builders accept it with options they don't support omitted
- Updated RQB filters to allow branded types in shortcut-form `eq` filter (fixes #5298)
- Fixed `$onUpdateFn` being executed without need (fixes #5780)
- Fixed `$onUpdateFn` potentially overriding explicit `null`s
- Fixed `zod` schema generator returning `unknown`-templated coerced types (fixes #5659)
- Fixed `mysql2` constructor setting param in potentially undefined mistyped config (fixes #5972)
- Fixed non-jit mapper nullification triggering on single null column (fixes #1603)
- Preserved qualifiers for column chunks of `sql` fields in selection when non-current table's column is referenced (fixes #5734) 
- Optimized query building, mapper generation
- Allowed empty returns in callback-style `orderBy`, `extras`, `RAW` of relational queries
- Removed unused `_` field in `RelationsHelperStatic`
- Fixed naming: `isReversed` to `isFilterReversed` in `Relation`
- `objects`, `arrays` `db.execute` modes (`db.all`, `db.get` in `sqlite`) (bypasses #4464)
- Fixed jit mapper nullifying nested selection objects with columns from different tables
- Fixed selection group nullification not triggering on objects with deeply nested fields (joined view or subquery)
- Fixed `geometry`, `geography` & `box` array types data getting reduced to one item due to wrong delimiter used during `pgArray` construction\parsing
- Added delimiter customization to `makePgArray`, `parsePgArray` utilities
- Optional explicit column lists for `db.insert` (workaround for #5001, #5309)
   - Usage: `db.insert(users, 'name', 'email').values([{ name: 'First', email: 'first@example.com' }, { name: 'Second', email: 'second@example.com' }])`
- Transaction snapshot support for `pg` dialect
- Fixed `pg` transaction config related errors on empty but present config (fixes #1772)
- Supported transaction config in effect `pg` drivers
- Bump `tursodatabase` library versions
- Supported transaction configs for `tursodatabase` drivers
- Fixed `mysql` transaction options being joined on wrong separator
- Supported `isolationLevel` in `bun-sql/mysql` transactions
- Removed transaction config from `effect-sqlite`, `effect-mysql` due to lack of support in drivers
- Explicit error throws on unsupported transaction configs
- Partial transaction config support for `libsql`, `tidb` drivers
- Improved error messages on unknown fields in RQBv2 selection (fixes #5367)
- Fixed `op-sqlite` transaction being handled as synchronous
- Fixed broken `op-sqlite` query executors (fixes #5936)
- Bumped `op-sqlite` to v17 (fixes #5928)
- Fixed `expo-sqlite` not finalizing prepared statements
- Added `expo-sqlite/async` for async querying (fixes #5240)
- Added local `sha256` hash function as a fallback for cache query hashing in environments without `globalThis.crypto` available
- Fixed dynamic query builders blocking query builder's variable reassignment after applying nullable joins by defaulting to `not-null` behavior on not yet joined column groups in selection (fixes #4232)
- Fixed `bytea` not being included in `pg` table creation callback format column list
- Moved `SQL.usedTables` calculation from constructor to getter
- Fixed false relation name collision error and relational filter misrouting for relation names shadowing `Object.prototype` properties like `constructor` (fixes #6076)
- Updated `neon-http` migrator to automatically rollback failed migrations
- Bump `effect` to `4.0.0` (fixes #6162, #6403, #6412)
- Improved hash for query name generation & query cache key
- Bump `typebox` to `1.2.0` (fixes #5981)
- Fixed internal type errors in built code
- Updated `mssql`, `cockroach`, `singlestore` sessions to new format
- Added missing `lateral` (`apply`), `cross` joins, `insert ... select`, `db.$count` to `mssql`
- Added explicit error on attempt to insert multiple default-only rows in `mssql`
- Fixed `blob` columns on React Native drivers: writes no longer require `Buffer`, `op-sqlite` and `expo-sqlite` reads normalized to `Uint8Array`. Use `blob(...).$type<UInt8Array>()` to override column's type
- Fixed cast codecs being applied to selection fields of inner queries in `pg`, `mysql`
- Fixed double space following `order by` in set operation queries
- Fixed `MSSQL`, `MySQL`, `SingleStore` `serial` types returning different types based on column's value
- Fixed `sqlite` generating `View`,`Subquery` queries with `cast` on `numeric` columns
- Codec system for `sqlite`, `cockroach`, `mssql`, `singlestore`
- Migrated `mssql`, `cockroach` to RQBv2
- Removed redundant `limit 1` from relational `where`, `coalesce` for json arrays in `sqlite` in RQBv2
- Removed RQBv1 `schema` from `DrizzleConfig`
- Fixed `mysql2` not using `codecs` from config over driver's default when provided
- Added delimiter customization to `makeCockroachArray`, `parseCockroachArray` utilities, mirroring their `pg` counterparts
- Fixed `cockroach` `geometry` arrays being unwritable due to wrong delimiter
- Fixed `cockroach` array parser dropping backslashes from string values
- Fixed `cockroach` `int4[]` being parsed to `string[]`
- Added `mapper` caching for queries reused without `.prepare()`
- Fixed table extra config not rejecting unsuitable for field values (fixes #6140)
- Fixed subquery derived from `.$dynamic()` query builder being unusable with `.from`, `.*Join` (fixes #4069)
- Fixed `Placeholder` `value` field described as `declare protected: TValue` instead of `declared protected value: TValue`; Set `name` field to `protected` and marked `getSQL` as `@deprecated` to prevent field from bleeding into relational filters' autocomplete 
- Fixed `Subquery.getSQL()` (fixes #2174)
- Fixed relational queries not supporting `Subquery` type fields in `View`s
- Fixed `alias` function returning materialized views typed as regular views
- Added typed `isAlias: boolean` type config property to `View`, `Table` to identify if it was aliased
- Added `isTableAlias`, `getTableSchema` utils, supported `View` in `getTableName` util
- Supported `Subquery` as relational entity in RQBv2: 
  - `Subquery` must have flat selection, same as `View`
  - Every used `Subquery` will be invoked only once in `WITH` section on root level of relational query, every reference will use it's alias
  - Same query can't have reference multiple `Subquery` instances with same alias
- Fixed excessive memory consumption on `mysql`, `mssql`, `singlestore` iterators 
- Fixed `mysql2` iterators leaving connection un-drained & deadlocked on errors 
- Fixed `mysql2` iterators hanging when connection is dropped mid-stream
- Fixed `ExtraConfigColumn.getSQL()` recursing into stack overflow (fixes #6050)
- Fixed `sqlite` dropping `| undefined` from `.get()` return type of `db.update(table).set(...).returning()`
- Fixed `sqlite` dropping `| undefined` from `.get()` return type of `db.insert(table).values(...).returning()` with `.onConflictDoNothing()` or `.onConflictSet({ where: ... })` present, `db.insert(table).select(...).returning()` (fixes #6107) 
- Fixed select codecs leaking into builders passed as sql operator argument  
- Fixed `undefined` = `null`, `bigint` = mimic `string`, different data view type collisions in `hashQuery` (fixes #5842)
- Fixed concurrent query + cache invalidation run (fixes #5828)
- Fixed cached query invalidation for: 
  - tables in nested SQL & subqueries
  - aliased and `tableCreator`-prefixed tables
  - tables defined on schemas
  - joined & aliased tables of query builders embedded into raw `sql`
  - tables used in filters, selected fields, order clause, set operators, CTE-s
- Added `getCacheKey(table)` util returning the name query cache tracks a table by (`schema.name`, or `name` for tables without schema; aliases resolve to their original tables)
- Fixed `orderBy` of set operations dropping table qualifiers in passed `sql` objects (e.g. `desc(column)`) 
- Supported `DSQL` adapters for `postgres-js` (`@aws/aurora-dsql-postgresjs-connector`) - `drizzle-orm/postgres-js/dsql`, `node-postgres` (`@aws/aurora-dsql-node-postgres-connector`) - `drizzle-orm/node-postgres/dsql` 
- Fixed param codecs getting applied to inlined params
- Reworked `db.execute` types (fixes #661):
  - Plain `db.execute(sql)` - returns union every possible response type by driver
  - `db.execute<never>(sql)` - returns rowless response type (i.e. `insert` without `returning`)
  - `db.execute<ReturnedObject>` - driver response with rows typed as `ReturnedObject[]` 
- Fixed `db.execute<IReturnedObject>(sql)` type template rejecting interfaces
- Typed `effect` drivers' raw `db.execute`, `db.run`   (fixes #6382)
- Fixed RQBv2 query config lacking type errors with `typescript@6` and above (fixes #5644, #6383)
- Fixed `mysql` `date` column being affected by server's timezone (fixes #1442)
- Fixed `effect-mysql`, `bun-sql/mysql` drivers losing `time` fraction   
- Fixed `SQLiteBigInt` attempting to use `Buffer` in encoder without `Buffer` present in environment (fixes #2043) 
- Fixed `durable-sqlite` `db.get(sql)` throwing on queries returning zero or more than one row instead of returning `undefined` or the first row
- Fixed `node-postgres` transaction crashing process if connection is dropped mid-transaction (fixes #6437)
- Fixed `node-postgres` transaction leaking the pool client on `BEGIN` error (fixes #6341)
- Fixed failed transaction `rollback` error replacing the original error that triggered it
- Added ordering by relations to RQBv2:
  ```typescript
  // Select users sorted by last post
  db.query.users.findMany({ orderBy: { posts: { createdAt: 'desc(max)' } } })

  // Select users sorted by post count
  db.query.users.findMany({ orderBy: { posts: 'asc(count)' } })
  
  // Select admin posts first, sort rest by creation date
  db.query.posts.findMany({ orderBy: { author: { isAdmin: 'desc' }, createdAt: 'desc' } })
  ```
- Added cache support to RQBv2 via `withCache` switch: 
  - `true` - cache query
  - `false` - never cache query
  - `undefined` - cache only with `all` cache strategy
  ```typescript
  db.query.users.findMany({ with: { posts: true }, withCache: true })
  ```
- Fixed `instanceof` not working reliably for `drizzle` classes in monorepos with multiple library instances  
- Fixed `aws-data-api/pg`:
  - Array params throwing `Unknown type` error - now sent as `pg` array literals
  - Object params throwing `Unknown type` error - now sent as JSON with `JSON` type hint
  - Multidimensional arrays in results being returned as raw `ArrayValue` objects
  - `char(n)` params being truncated to a single character by `::char` cast
  - `inet` values gaining full-width netmask (`/32`, `/128`) in results
  - `time({ withTimezone: true })` values losing their offset: params were cast to `::time`, results were converted to UTC by Data API
- Fixed `pg` `time({ withTimezone: true })` columns using `time` codecs instead of `timetz` ones
- Fixed [[BUG]: inArray/notInArray empty arrays do not work with SQL Server](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/5632)
- Fixed [[BUG]: node-postgres pool client is not released when transaction BEGIN rejects](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/6023)
- Fixed [Batch insert crashes with RangeError when row-count × column-count exceeds ~8 k rows × 15 cols (~120 k params)](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/5994)
- Fixed [[BUG]: Composition of not and or/and yields compile error](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/4160)
- Fixed [[BUG]: Negative limit not working in SQLite](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/2992)
- Fixed [[BUG]: Pooled transaction() leaks the pool client when BEGIN fails (node-postgres / neon-serverless / vercel-postgres)](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/6241)
- Fixed [[BUG]: node-postgres transaction() leaks the client on a rejected BEGIN and returns broken clients to the pool](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/6114). [node-postgres: transaction() runs BEGIN before try/finally, leaking the pool client when BEGIN fails](https://github.com/drizzle-team/drizzle-orm/issues/6341)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action required**
>
> - If you use ID token sign-in with a provider that has no `clientId`, set `clientId` to every client ID your apps sign in with. ([#11931](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11931))

## `better-auth`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed the JWT plugin to verify JWTs and session cookie-cache JWTs with the stored key's algorithm instead of the token header's, and to warn when signing or verifying a JWT without an issuer or audience ([#11925](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11925))
- Fixed OAuth callbacks completed through the OAuth proxy to run the same checks as the standard OAuth callback, including issuer and ID token nonce validation ([#11930](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11930))
- Fixed `auth.api.getSession()` to keep the original database error as `error.cause` when the session lookup fails ([#11924](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11924))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/29735514c737d2abeac2fb84f0691fd316231949/packages/better-auth/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/core`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed `mapProfileToUser` failing to typecheck under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` when it returns `undefined` for `name`, `email`, or `image` ([#11918](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11918))
- Fixed ID token sign-in to reject tokens when the provider has no client ID, since their audience cannot be checked ([#11931](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11931))
- Fixed a custom Facebook `getUserInfo` to no longer receive client-submitted access tokens issued to another Facebook app, and ID tokens missing `exp` or `iat` are now rejected ([#11919](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11919))
- Restored the Twitch and Paybin ID token handling from before 1.7.11, which made account info fail once the ID token stored at sign-in expired ([#11920](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11920))
- Added a `cause` option as a third argument to `APIError.from()` to keep the underlying error for server-side callers without exposing it in the response ([#11924](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11924))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/29735514c737d2abeac2fb84f0691fd316231949/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/mcp`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed `requireMcpAuth` to accept only OAuth access tokens and reject session JWTs from the JWT plugin, even when they share the issuer and audience ([#11934](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11934))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/29735514c737d2abeac2fb84f0691fd316231949/packages/mcp/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/sso`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed OIDC SSO sign-in to reject ID tokens missing `exp` or `iat` and providers with an empty client ID, matching social sign-in ([#11935](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11935))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/29735514c737d2abeac2fb84f0691fd316231949/packages/sso/CHANGELOG.md)

## Contributors

## `better-auth`

### ❗ Breaking Changes

- Changed the custom `DeviceAuthorizationGrant` interface for device-code approval ([#11610](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11610))
> **Migration:** Rename `assertSessionRedemption` to `assertStandaloneUse`, handle its new `use` argument, and remove uses of `getVerificationContext`, `verificationOpenAPIProperties`, and the interface's second type parameter.
- Fixed sign-up emails and OAuth session caching to run after database work completes ([#11751](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11751))
> **Migration:** Use a `databaseHooks.user.create.before` hook to reject sign-ups instead of throwing from `sendVerificationEmail` or `onExistingUserSignUp`, and account for logged cache-write failures no longer failing applicable sign-ins.
- Fixed concurrent device-code decisions so only the first approval or denial takes effect ([#11772](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11772))
> **Migration:** Replace checks for `device_code_already_processed` in `/device/approve` error types with checks for `invalid_request`.
- Fixed device-token polling to report `expired_token` immediately after a code expires ([#11772](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11772))
> **Migration:** Handle `expired_token` on the first poll after expiry rather than expecting an initial `slow_down` response.

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/f429179bcc0f690c78de0c92b57ce33e8e4215d9/packages/better-auth/CHANGELOG.md)

releases.body:
## :sparkles: Highlights

### :bar_chart: Chart component

A new [`Chart`](https://ui.nuxt.com/docs/components/chart) component built on [TanStack Charts](https://tanstack.com/charts/latest) renders `line`, `area`, `bar` and `donut` charts as an SVG on the server. Series colors follow your theme and color mode through the new `--ui-chart-*` CSS variables:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const data = [
  { month: 'January', desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: 'February', desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: 'March', desktop: 237, mobile: 120 }
]
</script>

<template>
  <UChart
    type="bar"
    :data="data"
    index="month"
    :categories="[{ key: 'desktop', label: 'Desktop' }, { key: 'mobile', label: 'Mobile' }]"
    stacked
  />
</template>
```

> [!NOTE]
> `@tanstack/charts` is an optional peer dependency, install it to use the component. When the props are not enough, the `definition` prop takes a full TanStack chart definition.

### :globe_with_meridians: Automatic locale with `@nuxtjs/i18n`

When `@nuxtjs/i18n` is installed, the [`App`](https://ui.nuxt.com/docs/components/app) component now follows the current i18n locale, and only the Nuxt UI locales matching your `i18n.locales` are bundled. You can drop the `import * as locales` pattern, which shipped every locale in the entry chunk:

```diff
- <script setup lang="ts">
- import * as locales from '@nuxt/ui/locale'
-
- const { locale } = useI18n()
- </script>
-
  <template>
-   <UApp :locale="locales[locale]">
+   <UApp>
      <NuxtPage />
    </UApp>
  </template>
```

> [!TIP]
> An explicit `locale` prop still wins, see the [i18n guide](https://ui.nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/integrations/i18n/nuxt#automatic-locale).

### :zap: Lighter and faster pages

Pages now load up to 27% less JavaScript. A page no longer loads the code of components only other pages use, and overlays are lazy loaded: the menu of `Header`, `Sidebar` and `DashboardSidebar`, the command palette of `DashboardSearch` and `ContentSearch`, and the toasts of `Toaster`.

| | v4.11.3 | v4.12.0 |
| --- | --: | --: |
| JS | 871.6 kB | 549.6 kB |
| JS (gzip) | 251.9 kB | 183.9 kB |

> [!NOTE]
> `UButton` also mounts about 38% faster and each item of an open `DropdownMenu` about 30% faster, since link props are now picked without a reactive proxy.

## `better-auth`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed Captcha and OpenAPI plugin subpath imports and type resolution for `better-auth/plugins/multi-session` and `better-auth/test`. ([#11822](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11822))
- Fixed Google One Tap sign-ins not recording `google` as the last login method. ([#11393](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11393))
- Fixed imports from `better-auth/plugins/one-tap` failing with a not-exported error. ([#11696](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11696))
- Fixed Google One Tap ignoring plugin-level `autoSelect` and `cancelOnTapOutside` settings. ([#11820](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11820))
- Fixed Google One Tap sign-ins ignoring configured Google profile mapping and user info updates. ([#11819](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11819))
- Fixed Google One Tap calling a prompt method unsupported by FedCM and retrying skipped prompts. ([#11821](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11821))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/6f08d6dc3276f0f3b2b2a4c6c114fb56caf1a4e3/packages/better-auth/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/oauth-provider`

### Features

- Added optional self-service signing key rotation for `private_key_jwt` clients. ([#11695](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11695))

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed valid DPoP proofs being rejected for parameterized routes and URLs with trailing slashes. ([#11786](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11786))
- Fixed native clients with HTTP loopback callbacks being rejected when application type inference is enabled. ([#11798](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11798))
- Fixed device-code clients being unable to refresh access for approved resources omitted from a token poll. ([#11815](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11815))
- Fixed OAuth consent without a reference overwriting or reusing consent for a different reference. ([#11801](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11801))
- Fixed dynamic client registration rejecting requests that include both supported and unsupported grants. ([#11797](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11797))
- Fixed attempts to change cached trusted clients returning HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 400. ([#11781](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11781))
- Improved errors for unknown OAuth `client_id` values to say `client not found`. ([#11799](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11799))
- Fixed PKCE verifier errors to return the specified HTTP 400 response and error code. ([#11724](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11724))
- Fixed unknown OAuth clients receiving `invalid_grant` instead of `invalid_client` at the token endpoint. ([#11176](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11176))
- Fixed unverifiable JWT access tokens causing server errors at `/oauth2/userinfo`, `/oauth2/introspect`, and `/oauth2/revoke`. ([#11596](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11596))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/6f08d6dc3276f0f3b2b2a4c6c114fb56caf1a4e3/packages/oauth-provider/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/core`

### Bug Fixes

- Limited JWKS refetches for unknown key IDs to protect servers from repeated requests. ([#11805](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11805))
- Fixed unreachable JWKS endpoints being reported as invalid tokens instead of server errors. ([#11612](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11612))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/6f08d6dc3276f0f3b2b2a4c6c114fb56caf1a4e3/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/mongo-adapter`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed MongoDB `findMany` ignoring ID sorting and potentially repeating or skipping paginated results. ([#11801](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11801))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/6f08d6dc3276f0f3b2b2a4c6c114fb56caf1a4e3/packages/mongo-adapter/CHANGELOG.md)

## Contributors

@Bekacru, @breken-ai, @drewsephski, @gustavovalverde, @mahoor, @vhinayindia

releases.name: v4.6.0
releases.body: > v4.6.0 is the next minor release. ## 📣 Some news ### 🖥️ Nuxt CLI v4 Alongside the release of Nuxt v4.6, today also brings a new major release of the Nuxt CLI: **`@nuxt/cli` v4**. It ships as a dependency of `nuxt`, so you'll get it automatically when you upgrade. Most of what's new is in `nuxt dev`: - **an interactive terminal UI**, showing URLs, startup progress and keyboard shortcuts, with panels to dive into error logs, routes, network requests and more - **the dev server gives you more info**, such as why it reloaded or restarted, which `nuxt.config` keys changed, where the time went during a slow start or build, and how long each module took to set up - **a CLI-level error channel** rendered with `my-bad` (see below), powering things like automatically reloading when a syntax error in `nuxt.config.ts` is fixed - **a lock file** in `.nuxt/`, which lets a second `nuxt dev` (say, one started by an agent) take over or defer to the one you started, and powers new `nuxt curl` and `nuxt task` commands that talk to the running server There's also a new `nuxt docs ""` search, and `nuxt preview --takeover` can replace a running preview server. And in general `nuxt/cli` is a ***lot*** smaller and starts a ***lot*** faster: | | v3.37 | v4.0 | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `@nuxt/cli` install size | 13.1 MB | 3.5 MB | **-73%** | | `@nuxt/cli` dependencies | 70 | 31 | **-56%** | | `nuxt dev`: first paint | 330 ms | 50 ms | **6.6x faster** | | `nuxt dev`: port bound | 338 ms | 104 ms | **3.2x faster** | | `nuxt dev`: memory at rest (Linux) | 630 MB | 440 MB | **-30%** | Although this is a major version, none of the changes should be breaking for Nuxt v4 users: we require Node.js v22.21+, v24.11+ or v26+, we drop `nuxt init` and only support `npm create nuxt@latest`, and Nuxt 2 and `@nuxt/bridge` are no longer supported. 👉 **Check out the full [Nuxt CLI v4 release notes](https://github.com/nuxt/cli/releases/tag/v4.0.0) for everything that's changed.** ### 💡 A server-agnostic Nuxt The biggest thing about this release is our move towards making Nuxt server-agnostic. I feel that freedom of choice is very much a fundamental value of the web, and one that unites the whole Nuxt team. You can use `pages/` (with vue-router) or not. You can use Vite, webpack or Rspack to bundle your code. You can pick from dozens of providers to deploy to, pick any image or font provider, choose any database adapter. In every case, the framework is the same. The server side was different. `#app` composables imported h3 types, server code imported from `h3` and `nitropack`, and every module that touched the server was tied to whichever major version of those packages Nuxt happened to depend on. This has become particularly clear as we have been upgrading to new majors of h3 and nitro, which ship breaking changes with a cascading effect throughout the whole ecosystem. 👉 **This release changes that.** Alongside explicitly defining our public API in `nuxt/kit` (which now does not refer to external packages), Nuxt now specifies our own types for the request event, route rules and typed `$fetch`, and we expose an import surface (`nuxt/server`) for the server utilities that will be needed by most apps. This is the culmination of work we started almost a year ago, making it possible to use any server builder with Nuxt, not just Nitro ([#33462](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/33462)). Of course, under the hood, `nuxt/server` is still powered by Nitro by default - though we are also announcing a second, experimental implementation, `@nuxt/vite-server`, which allows pure-Vite server builds using the [Vite Environment API](https://vite.dev/guide/api-environment#environment-api). > [!IMPORTANT] > We believe that Nitro is still the right choice for almost everyone. 🌟 We see a number of key benefits for `nuxt/server`. 1. **it smooths the upgrade to Nuxt 5**, which moves to Nitro v3 and h3 v2. Server code written against `nuxt/server` on 4.6 runs unchanged there, so a module can ship one file for both. 2. **it decouples Nuxt from the Nitro release cycle**. Because we 'own' the API, we can adapt to breaking changes in Nitro or h3 without requiring a future major - and we can release Nuxt majors without having to wait for upstream releases. 3. **it makes Nuxt's code more maintainable**. It helps us preserve the separation of concerns between our API - `/app` and `/server` - and the bundler + server that you ultimately want to build your app. ... and there are a number of other benefits too, from a single type surface to being able to iterate more quickly on features. Finally, I want to say a special thank-you to [@pi0](https://github.com/pi0), whose relentless focus on server agnosticism and work on h3, Nitro and web-standard server primitives over the last few years is what makes a portable `RequestEvent` possible at all. Thank you, Pooya. ❤️ Almost every feature in this release is already in the Nuxt 5 branch, and most of the remaining Nuxt 5 defaults can be tested today with `future.compatibilityVersion: 5` (more details below!). > [!TIP] > Nuxt 3 reached end-of-life on July 31, 2026, so there is no 3.x release alongside this one. If you're still on v3, the [upgrade guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/upgrade) is waiting for you. ## 👀 Highlights 🤷 If you've read this far I'm afraid I have bad news for you: there's a lot more still to say! Nuxt 4.6 is one of our biggest minor releases, with over 420 commits since v4.5.2. ... so, you might want to grab a coffee! ☕️ ### 🧩 `nuxt/server` It has been asked for for a long time, and it now exists ([#36275](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36275))! `nuxt/server` is a new import source for server code: handlers, middleware and utilities - a complement to `nuxt/app`. Where `nuxt/app` is for the part of your application that also runs in the browser, `nuxt/server` is for the part that only runs on the server. ```ts [server/api/hello.ts] import { defineEventHandler, getQuery } from 'nuxt/server' export default defineEventHandler((event) => { const { name } = getQuery<{ name?: string }>(event) return { message: `Hello, ${name ?? 'world'}!` } }) ``` The utilities use web standards and are typed against a portable `RequestEvent`: ```ts event.req // Request event.url // URL event.res // { status, statusText, headers } event.res.headers // Headers event.context // per-request context ``` Under `@nuxt/nitro-server` they are backed by Nitro and h3, but you never import from either. So the same handler runs under Nitro v2, Nitro v3 or `@nuxt/vite-server`, and a module that imports from `nuxt/server` doesn't need a peer dependency on `h3` or `nitropack`. We think this will make a big difference in smoothing out the upgrade to Nuxt v5 and Nitro v3. There is a typing benefit too. We no longer hoist h3 or Nitro types into your app to type `useRequestEvent`, `$fetch` or route rules, which removes a source of type conflicts when versions differ ([#36212](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36212), [#36214](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36214), [#36293](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36293)). The surface is small, and covers what published modules and user code typically need: `defineEventHandler`, `createError`/`isNuxtError`, request URL, headers, query, body (plain and validated with any [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev) library or a function), cookies, redirects, response status, `getRouterParam(s)`, `getRequestIP`, `handleCors`, `getRouteRules`, `useRuntimeConfig`, `useAppConfig` and sessions. ```ts [server/api/users.post.ts] import { defineEventHandler, readValidatedBody } from 'nuxt/server' import { z } from 'zod' export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => { const user = await readValidatedBody(event, z.object({ name: z.string() })) return { created: user.name } }) ``` We encourage you to use web APIs (`event.req.headers`, for example), or raise an issue if there's functionality you're missing from `nuxt/server` 🙏 If you do need to step outside `nuxt/server` for a particular handler, don't worry! Nothing has been taken away: import `defineEventHandler` and the helpers you need from `h3` or `nitropack/runtime` as before, and that handler works exactly as it did on Nuxt 4.5. ```ts [server/api/upload.post.ts] import { defineEventHandler, readMultipartFormData } from 'h3' export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => { const parts = await readMultipartFormData(event) return { received: parts?.length ?? 0 } }) ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > On Nuxt 4, the _auto-imported_ `defineEventHandler`, `getQuery`, `readBody` and the rest are still h3's own helpers, which take a different shape of event. Import from `nuxt/server` explicitly, including `defineEventHandler` to use the new server runtime. If you mix the two, you'll see a `NUXT_E8012` error which should tell you which import to change. A few helpers also behave differently from their h3 v1 namesakes: `sendRedirect` returns the response rather than sending it, `createError` takes `status` and `statusText`, and response headers are set through `event.res.headers`. The upgrade guide has [a table of the differences](https://nuxt.com/docs/getting-started/upgrade#moving-to-nuxtserver). Nothing in this release _requires_ a migration. But if you have server code you'd like to make portable ahead of Nuxt 5, this is the best way. 👉 Read the [server imports guide](https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/going-further/server-imports). ### 🔐 `appSecret` and sessions Nuxt now has a root application secret: `runtimeConfig.appSecret`, set with `NUXT_APP_SECRET` ([#35874](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35874), thanks to [@onmax](https://github.com/onmax)). Modules and server features derive purpose-specific secrets from it with `deriveSecret(purpose)`, so `NUXT_APP_SECRET` is the only secret you need to configure. ```bash openssl rand -base64 32 ``` In development Nuxt generates and persists one if none is configured (and warns the first time a derived secret is used). Builds never generate one. The first thing to use it is a set of session helpers in `nuxt/server` ([#36358](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36358)). Sessions are sealed into a cookie with [iron](https://github.com/brc-dd/iron-webcrypto), so there's no server-side storage to configure: ```ts [server/api/visits.ts] import { defineEventHandler, useSession } from 'nuxt/server' export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => { const session = await useSession<{ visits: number }>(event) await session.update(data => ({ visits: (data.visits ?? 0) + 1 })) return { visits: session.data.visits } }) ``` > [!NOTE] > As a reminder, runtime config keys prefixed with `app` (`runtimeConfig.app`, `runtimeConfig.appSecret`) are reserved for Nuxt. ### 🎯 Typed `$fetch`, rebuilt `$fetch` and `useFetch` have been typed from your server routes for a long time. But the types were derived from Nitro's `InternalApi` interface, and past a few hundred routes they hit TypeScript's instantiation limit with the familiar `TS2589: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite`. We've rebuilt typed fetch on top of [`fetchdts`](https://github.com/danielroe/fetchdts) ([#36238](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36238)). Nuxt compiles your server routes into a route tree with an exact-match table for static paths and accessors specialised to your route set. Resolution cost now scales with call sites, not with route count: | routes | before | after | | - | - | - | | 100 | 1,397,361 instantiations / 0.77s | 51,558 / 0.26s | | 300 | 5,774,425 / 3.49s (`TS2589`) | 51,558 / 0.16s | | 1000 | 12,831,467 / 7.44s (`TS2589`) | 51,558 / 0.20s | | 3000 (200 call sites) | 71,875,148 / 53.63s (`TS2589`) | 101,678 / 0.62s | Peak memory for the same runs dropped from 946 MB to 140 MB. 🔥 Plus, the route set also carries the `body`, `query` and `headers` a handler validates, so calls are checked more tightly than before: ```ts // server/api/users.post.ts validates { title: string, count: number } await $fetch('/api/users', { method: 'post', body: { title: 'a', count: 1 } }) await $fetch('/api/users', { method: 'post', body: { title: 'a', count: 'no' } }) // ^ not assignable to number await $fetch('/api/users', { method: 'post' }) // ^ body is required ``` On Nuxt 4 this is opt-in, because there are small changes to type inference, and hand-written `ServerRoutes` augmentations need a small rewrite. It is the default in Nuxt 5. ```ts [nuxt.config.ts] export default defineNuxtConfig({ experimental: { routeTypedFetch: true, }, }) ``` There's also a new `experimental.strictRouteTypes` option to reject calls to paths that don't exist (otherwise these just return `unknown`), and an `'isomorphic'` mode that types your pages as `GET` routes too if you want to be able to `$fetch` from the Vue renderer with type safety. 👉 Read more in the [experimental features docs](https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/going-further/experimental-features#routetypedfetch). ### 🐛 Better errors in development with `my-bad` Server-side errors in development used to look like this: ``` ReferenceError: foo is not defined at Object. (/_nuxt/app/pages/index.vue:1:1) ``` There was no source position or code frame, and the Youch iframe we rendered could not show you the frame in your own source either. Both are now fixed ([#36258](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36258), [nuxt/cli#1518](https://github.com/nuxt/cli/pull/1518)). Dev SSR stack traces are now mapped before anything reads the error, and the Youch overlay has been replaced with [`my-bad`](https://github.com/danielroe/my-bad). It renders into your app's own error page as an overlay (or as a standalone page when the app can't render one), with the mapped stack trace and a code frame from your source, and the same report is printed in your terminal. We are still working with [@atinux](https://github.com/atinux), [@HugoRCD](https://github.com/HugoRCD) and [@antfu](https://github.com/antfu) to make these pages nicer still. With Nuxt CLI v4, there is a single live error channel at the CLI level. It survives worker restarts, so (for example) a syntax error in `nuxt.config.ts` will live-reload the page once you fix it. Each error is rendered once rather than at every layer it passes through, and the same channel streams build progress and app logs to the dev panel. ### 🎨 A new loading screen, 404 and error pages [@HugoRCD](https://github.com/HugoRCD) has redrawn the loading screen you see while the dev server starts. It is now a WebGL2 particle field that traces a mountain range behind the Nuxt lockup ([#36178](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36178)), using a single shader and a single draw call. Without WebGL2 it falls back to the static lockup, and with `prefers-reduced-motion` the animation stops. Try hovering over it. 🏔️ Hugo also gave the built-in 404 and error pages a neutral palette and lighter type ([#36255](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36255)), and [@MirkoJa](https://github.com/MirkoJa) added a back button to the 404 page ([#35688](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35688)). ### ⚡️ Vue Vapor support Nuxt now supports Vue 3.6's [Vapor Mode](https://github.com/vuejs/core/releases/tag/v3.6.0-rc.1#about-vapor-mode) in interop mode ([#35759](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35759)). Your app root stays on the virtual DOM, and you can opt individual components or pages into Vapor by adding the `vapor` attribute to ` ``` Routing, `useAsyncData`, layouts and most built-in components keep working unchanged. Along the way we made the auto-import loader, `useAsyncData`, `definePageMeta` and slot inspection Vapor-aware, and we now have a Vapor test suite so we can track what's supported. > [!NOTE] > This requires Vue `^3.6.0-rc.2` or newer. See the [known limitations](https://nuxt.com/docs/guide/concepts/vuejs-development#known-limitations) and try it in a fresh project first. ### 🧩 Addons for `useFetch` and `useAsyncData` [@cernymatej](https://github.com/cernymatej) has added an `addons` option to the `createUseFetch` and `createUseAsyncData` factories ([#35797](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35797)). An addon can declare custom call-site options, adjust the merged options, wrap the handler with middleware, and extend what the composable returns, and it can be reused across as many custom instances as you like. ```ts [app/composables/useApiFetch.ts] const refreshOnFocus = defineUseFetchAddon({ setup: (options: UseFetchAddonOptions<{ refreshOnFocus?: boolean }>) => { if (import.meta.server || !options.refreshOnFocus) { return } return (asyncData) => { const focused = useWindowFocus() watch(focused, focused => focused && asyncData.refresh()) return { focused } } }, }) export const useApiFetch = createUseFetch({ baseURL: '/api', addons: [refreshOnFocus] }) ``` ```vue [app/pages/todos.vue] ``` This resolves a long list of feature requests for `useAsyncData` and `useFetch` (refresh on focus, polling, retries, auth headers and more) without making the core composables opinionated about any of them. 👉 Read about [`defineUseFetchAddon`](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/utils/define-use-fetch-addon) and [`defineUseAsyncDataAddon`](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/utils/define-use-async-data-addon). ### 🚀 Performance There is a lot of performance work in this release. - **`` renders 58% faster on the server** ([#36015](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36015)). Internal links are now rendered as a plain `` with no `useLink`, no computed and no reactive state. Rendering 200 links went from 1.36ms to 0.57ms, which is 1.4x faster than a bare ``. - **Early 404s** ([#36117](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36117)). With `experimental.early404`, page routes are compiled into a static matcher at build time and requests that can't match any page skip creating the Vue app, running plugins and middleware entirely. On an app with 30 pages and ~23ms of boot work per render, a JSON 404 went from 37.1ms to 0.3ms. - **Templates declare their dependencies** ([#35875](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35875)). The virtual file templates used in Nuxt's build used to regenerate on every file change. They now declare what invalidates them, so editing a component regenerates 0 of 49 core templates instead of all of them, and the `builder:watch` hook settles in 0.6ms instead of 36ms. - **Cookie jars** ([#36114](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36114)). `useCookie` parses the cookie header once per request (or once per microtask on the client) instead of on every call. A nice side effect: a cookie set in a plugin during SSR can now be read by a later `useCookie` in a page. - **`ssr: false` pages are tree-shaken from the server bundle** ([#35836](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35836), thanks to [@Austin1serb](https://github.com/Austin1serb)). - **Serializable `definePageMeta` keys are extracted at build time** ([#35919](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35919)), behind `experimental.extractSerializablePageMeta`. - **Faster dev server warm-up**: Vite's server module graph is warmed before the client ([#36154](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36154)), the client graph is crawled during warm-up ([#35870](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35870)), and warm-up yields to your first navigation so it never competes with a real request ([#36412](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36412)). - **Smaller client bundle**: `unctx` is no longer shipped to the browser and `defu` is skipped for a single `app.config` ([#36371](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36371)). - **Fewer dependencies**: `@nuxt/kit` no longer depends on `c12`, `untyped`, `confbox`, `pkg-types`, `ufo` or `mlly`, and `jiti` and `giget` are now optional peers loaded only when needed ([#35936](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35936), [#35943](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35943), [#35946](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35946), [#36071](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36071), [#36073](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36073), [#36083](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36083)). - Lazy impound tracing for builds ([#36172](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36172)), virtual module hooks filtered by id ([#36077](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36077)), `isVue` checks migrated to plugin filters ([#36116](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36116)) and an `flru` prerender cache ([#36340](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36340)). Put together, on our benchmark machine (arm64 Linux, Node 24.15, medians of 5 runs): | | v4.5.2 | v4.6.0 | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `@nuxt/kit` install size | 6.4 MB | 2.1 MB | **-67%** | | `@nuxt/kit` transitive dependencies | 36 | 22 | **-39%** | | `nuxt build`, starter | 4.4 s | 3.6 s | **-18%** | | `nuxt build`, 200 pages / 200 components / 50 routes | 11.6 s | 10.3 s | **-11%** | | SSR throughput, page with 300 ``s | 110 req/s | 140 req/s | **+26%** | Dev server start-up (spawn to first HTML) on the same machine is about 12% faster on a starter app, with the second request served in roughly half the time, though the CLI major changed alongside so not all of that is Nuxt. ### 📦 Lighter payloads `useAsyncData` and `useFetch` accept a `serialize: false` option to keep data out of the `__NUXT_DATA__` payload ([#35779](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35779)). That's most useful inside components that never hydrate, and `experimental.stripNeverHydratedData` applies it automatically to data fetched within `hydrate-never` component trees. Nuxt also warns in development when a page's payload exceeds 100 kB ([#35777](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35777)) and when a route rendered with `noScripts` relies on client-side JavaScript ([#35780](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35780)), and `noScripts` pages keep their non-script resource hints and attach their styles correctly ([#35803](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35803), [#36356](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36356), [#36359](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36359)). `` now prefetches server-page islands ([#35808](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35808)), and [@atinux](https://github.com/atinux) made prefetch hints throttled and prioritised so a page full of links doesn't flood the network ([#36261](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36261), [#36324](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36324)). Building on that, route chunks, layouts, middleware, payloads, islands and resource hints all now go through one client prefetch scheduler with per-kind concurrency caps, deduplication by key, and cancellation of in-flight work when you navigate away ([#36391](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36391)). ### 🔮 Nuxt 5 features, today Most of what's new in Nuxt 5 is already in 4.6, either as the default or behind a flag. `future.compatibilityVersion: 5` turns on the Nuxt 5 defaults in one go, and every one of them can be enabled (or disabled) individually. ```ts [nuxt.config.ts] export default defineNuxtConfig({ future: { compatibilityVersion: 5, }, }) ``` Newly gated behind the flag in this release: - **Typed pages** (`experimental.typedPages`) ([#35789](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35789)) - **Typed `$fetch`** (`experimental.routeTypedFetch`), described above - **Case-sensitive routing**, matching Nitro ([#35650](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/35650), thanks to [@Mateleo](https://github.com/Mateleo)) - **Early return from `navigateTo`** (`experimental.navigateToEarlyReturn`): `navigateTo` in `

releases.name: v3.0.260903-beta
releases.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Thi release focuses on security hardenings, bug fixes, better observability, and a more reliable development experience.

Many of new improvements are from major dependency upgrades (h3, srvx, rou3, ocache, db0, env-runner, unctx and unwasm) plus the work in Nitro to adopt them. The sections below group the changes by what they mean for your app.

## 🚀 What’s new

### 🧭 Routing and route rules

Nitro migrated to the new route rules engine from h3, backed by [rou3 v0.9](https://github.com/h3js/rou3/releases/tag/v0.9.0). See the [Nitro routing guide](https://nitro.build/docs/routing) and [h3 route rules guide](https://h3.dev/guide/rules). ([#4411](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4411))

- Rules are matched on the canonical path, with sibling routes ordered by specificity. ([#4396](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4396))
- `GET` routes automatically answer `HEAD` requests.
- New `cors` rule replaces manual CORS wiring: `{ "/api/**": { cors: true } }`.
- `basicAuth` route rules are replaced by middleware (see [After you upgrade](#-after-you-upgrade)).

### 💾 Caching

`defineCachedHandler`, `defineCachedFunction` and `cache` route rules now run on [ocache v0.3](https://github.com/unjs/ocache/releases/tag/v0.3.0) (up from 0.1), which brings safer defaults, bounded memory and several new capabilities. **Please review your caching configuration** — defaults changed. See [Review your caching configuration](#review-your-caching-configuration) and the [Nitro caching guide](https://nitro.build/docs/cache).

### 🗄️ Database

Nitro now uses [db0 v0.4](https://github.com/unjs/db0/releases/tag/v0.4.0). Database client libraries are passed explicitly to connectors; Nitro handles this for configured connectors and prompts to install what is missing. New in this line: `neon`, `prisma` and `libsql-core` connectors, Kysely integration, database `capabilities` metadata, and tracing channel support. See the [Nitro database guide](https://nitro.build/docs/database), [db0 connectors](https://db0.unjs.io/connectors), and [db0 integrations](https://db0.unjs.io/integrations).

### 🔌 WebSockets

WebSocket support moves to [crossws 0.4.12](https://github.com/h3js/crossws/releases) (from 0.4.6), which adds a batch of features usable from Nitro WebSocket handlers. See the [Nitro WebSocket guide](https://nitro.build/docs/websocket).

- **Liveness:** universal `idleTimeout` to detect half-open connections, application-level ping/pong hooks and `peer.ping()`. ([#201](https://github.com/h3js/crossws/pull/201), [#202](https://github.com/h3js/crossws/pull/202))
- **Backpressure:** `peer.bufferedAmount` ([docs](https://crossws.h3.dev/guide/peer#peerbufferedamount)) and opt-in subprotocol negotiation. ([#195](https://github.com/h3js/crossws/pull/195), [#203](https://github.com/h3js/crossws/pull/203))
- **Pub/sub:** a sync backplane to share channels across instances ([docs](https://crossws.h3.dev/guide/sync)), plus auth and context support. ([#192](https://github.com/h3js/crossws/pull/192), [#112](https://github.com/h3js/crossws/pull/112))

### 🔭 Observability and tracing

- **Native platform traces:** Nitro sends spans to [Vercel session traces](https://vercel.com/docs/tracing/session-tracing) and [Cloudflare Workers Observability](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/custom-spans/) without bundling the OpenTelemetry SDK. ([#4355](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4355), [#4413](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4413))
- **Built-in tracing logger:** enable [`tracingChannel`](https://nitro.build/config#tracingchannel) and `experimental.tracingLogger` to log completed h3, srvx, unstorage, db0 and other spans in development and production — without additional dependencies. ([#4406](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4406))

### 🔒 Security

- h3 has undergone several rounds of security hardening audits (path normalization, forwarded headers, host header handling, cookies, CORS, basic auth, JSON-RPC, session sealing).
- Development task endpoints (`/_nitro/tasks` and `/_nitro/tasks/:name`) now accept only local requests. This prevents remote clients with access to the dev server from listing or invoking tasks. ([#4389](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4389))
- Cached responses no longer replay cookies by default.
- **Better static file responses:** conditional requests with `ETag` and `Last-Modified`, byte ranges, optional `Cache-Control`, and additional path-traversal hardening.

### ⚡ Faster and more reliable

- Improved alias resolution, development sourcemaps, request middleware, and logging.
- Development worker reloads are serialized and cleanly awaited, stale module caches are cleared, (vite) aliases apply in the correct order, base paths are respected, and `?import` requests remain handled by Vite.
- Static presets no longer create an unnecessary server bundle.

#### 📁 Import any file as bytes or text

In server bundle: ([#4431](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4431))

```ts
  import logo from "./logo.png" with { type: "bytes" }; // Uint8Array
  import readme from "./README.md" with { type: "text" }; // string
```

### 📦 No more peer dependencies

Nitro no longer has **any** peer dependencies. Features that need an extra package (a builder, a preset, a storage driver, a database connector) resolve it **from your project**, and Nitro prompts to install anything missing. In CI, missing packages are installed automatically. Existing projects need no changes when the required packages are already installed. ([#4542](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4542), [#4543](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4543))

Nitro also validates the version of what it finds and warns when an installed package is outside the supported range. Supported builders are `vite@^7 || ^8`, `rollup@^4` and `rolldown@>=1.0.0`. ([87219b2](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/commit/87219b2a))

### Leaner install

Alongside dropping peer dependencies, several packages were removed from Nitro entirely: `tsconfck` (replaced by `get-tsconfig`), `magic-string`, `uncrypto`, `serve-placeholder`, `edge-runtime`, `@types/http-proxy` and `@types/node-fetch`. `ofetch` is no longer a runtime dependency, and `rou3` is now a direct dependency instead of being pulled in indirectly.

### ☁️ Presets

- **Cloudflare:** local development now uses Miniflare/`workerd` directly, with bindings available on the request event. Nitro offers to install `miniflare` when first needed. See the [Nitro Cloudflare guide](https://nitro.build/deploy/providers/cloudflare). ([#4338](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4338))
- **Vercel:** set `vercel.immutableStaticFiles: true` to emit content-hashed static files with immutable caching. See the [Nitro Vercel guide](https://nitro.build/deploy/providers/vercel#immutable-static-files). ([#4432](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4432))
- **Netlify Edge:** keeps dynamic imports lazy, reducing cold-start work for lazy handlers and deferred WASM initialization. ([#4525](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4525))

## ⚠️ Migration

### Routing

- **Replace `basicAuth` route rules with middleware.**

  ```ts [routes/admin/index.ts]
  import { defineHandler } from "nitro";
  import { basicAuth } from "nitro/h3";

  export default defineHandler({
    middleware: [basicAuth({ username: "admin", password: "supersecret" })],
    handler: (event) => `Hello, ${event.context.basicAuth?.username}!`,
  });
  ```

  To protect multiple routes, register route-scoped middleware or add it under `middleware/`.

- **Use the new `cors` rule** where needed: `{ "/api/**": { cors: true } }`.
- **Update renamed types when convenient:** `NitroRouteConfig` and `NitroRouteRules` are deprecated aliases for `RouteRuleConfig` and `NormalizedRouteRules`. The old names are still exported from `nitro/types`.

### Review your caching configuration

The upgrade from ocache 0.1 to 0.3 introduces safer defaults for `defineCachedHandler`, `defineCachedFunction`, and `cache` route rules:

- `swr` now defaults to `false`, so expired entries are refreshed before returning. Set `swr: true` to keep background revalidation. The `swr` route-rule shortcut already does this.
- Query parameters are ignored by default. Set `allowQuery: true` or list the parameters that should affect the cache key.
- Cookies are removed from cached requests and responses unless listed in `allowCookies`; responses containing `Set-Cookie` are not cached.
- `GET` and `HEAD` now use separate cache entries.
- Cache keys now include the request authority, and undeclared request headers are hidden from handlers.
- Cache resolution has a new 30-second timeout (`maxResolveTime`), and memory storage is limited by bytes.

See the [ocache migration guide](https://ocache.unjs.io/docs/migration) for details.

---

## 📦 Major dependency updates

| Package | From | To | Release notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `h3` | `2.0.1-rc.22` | `^2.0.1-rc.29` | [rc.23](https://github.com/h3js/h3/releases/tag/v2.0.1-rc.23) … [rc.29](https://github.com/h3js/h3/releases/tag/v2.0.1-rc.29) |
| `srvx` | `^0.11.16` | `^0.12.7` | [v0.12.0](https://github.com/h3js/srvx/releases/tag/v0.12.0) |

### `h3`

- **New route rules engine** ([#1524](https://github.com/h3js/h3/pull/1524), [docs](https://h3.dev/guide/rules)) — what Nitro's route rules now build on.
- **New request features:** `QUERY` method support, automatic `HEAD` matching for `GET` routes, `requireContentType` and `appendAcceptQuery`, `formdata` in `readBody`, async validation in `defineValidatedHandler`, an `onDispose` hook, and returning an `EventStream` directly from handlers. See the [h3 request utilities](https://h3.dev/utils/request).
- **Sessions:** default `SameSite=Lax` cookie, PBKDF2 seal iterations raised to 8192, and opt-in `idleTimeout` for sliding expiration. See the [h3 session example](https://h3.dev/examples/handle-session).
- **Performance:** precomposed middleware chains, streaming body-limit enforcement, faster path normalization and cookie parsing.
- **Security:** escaped interpolation in the `html` template tag, hop-aware `x-forwarded-*` handling, host header no longer steers the synthesized URL, stricter percent-decoding and canonical-path checks in static serving, hardened basic auth and JSON-RPC, and safer CORS `Vary`/credential handling. See the [h3 security utilities](https://h3.dev/utils/security).

### `srvx`

- **Static files:** security hardening, `ETag` + `Last-Modified` conditional requests, byte-range support, and opt-in `Cache-Control` via `maxAge`/`immutable`. ([#252](https://github.com/h3js/srvx/pull/252), [#269](https://github.com/h3js/srvx/pull/269), [#273](https://github.com/h3js/srvx/pull/273), [#275](https://github.com/h3js/srvx/pull/275))
- **Performance:** the middleware chain is precomposed at construction time and stdout writes are batched with a cached timestamp.
- **Node adapter correctness:** bridged responses stream instead of buffering, hop-by-hop headers are stripped, `HEAD` bodies are discarded, client aborts destroy the body stream, and unhandled handler errors answer `500`.
- **New:** body size limit helpers via `srvx/body-limit` ([docs](https://srvx.h3.dev/guide/body-limit)).
- ⚠️ Subpath exports were renamed to `*Middleware` / `*Plugin` ([#278](https://github.com/h3js/srvx/pull/278)).

### `rou3`

- Route pattern **overlap utilities** ([#183](https://github.com/h3js/rou3/pull/183)) and `regExpToRoute()` to convert PCRE regex back to a route pattern ([#188](https://github.com/h3js/rou3/pull/188)).
- `findAllRoutes` aligned with `findRoute` and compiled `matchAll`, with same-node siblings ordered by specificity.

### `db0`

See the [Nitro database guide](https://nitro.build/docs/database) and the [db0 connector reference](https://db0.unjs.io/connectors).

- ⚠️ **Connectors require the client library to be passed explicitly.** Nitro does this for connectors you configure, and prompts to install the missing package.
- New `neon` (serverless postgres), `prisma` and `libsql-core` connectors, plus a **Kysely** integration.
- Database `capabilities` metadata and exposed connector name.
- Tracing channel support (feeds the new tracing logger).
- ⚠️ Drizzle upgraded to **v1**, with `schema` parameter support and updated postgres/mysql connectors.

### `ocache`

See the [Nitro caching guide](https://nitro.build/docs/cache) and [ocache migration guide](https://ocache.unjs.io/docs/migration).

New in this line, beyond the default changes listed above:

- **Layered and binary-friendly storage:** `composeStorage` for fast + persistent backends, native binary payloads without base64, binary function results, and `createBlobStorage`.
- **Latency and background work:** opt into `stream` to serve a cache fill while it is still buffering, and `waitUntil` for background tasks.
- **New hooks and options:** `getMaxAge` (per-entry TTL), `serialize`, `shouldCache`, async `validate`, `sendCacheControl: false`, and `.expire()` / `.invalidate()` / `.resolveKeys()` on cached handlers.
- **Automatic headers:** `Vary` emission for your `varies` config and an `x-cache` status header (`hit` / `stale` / `revalidated` / `miss`).
- **Runtime-independent hashing:** deterministic SHA-256 based hashing with stronger collision protection and no runtime dependencies.

### `env-runner`

See the [Nitro Cloudflare guide](https://nitro.build/deploy/providers/cloudflare#local-preview).

- ⚠️ Runtime dependencies are now explicit — Nitro offers to install `miniflare` the first time Cloudflare local development needs it.

### `unctx` (async context)

- Defaults to the built-in `AsyncLocalStorage`.
- Transform moved to **oxc**, skips files without `await`, and precomputes line offsets.
- Fixes an instance leak via `AsyncLocalStorage` using `WeakRef`.

### `unwasm` (WASM support)

See the [unwasm documentation](https://github.com/unjs/unwasm#readme).

- ⚠️ `webassemblyjs` replaced with a **built-in WASM parser** ([#104](https://github.com/unjs/unwasm/pull/104)) — fewer dependencies and a lighter install.

It scans your source and only generates the theme CSS for the components you use: ```ts [vite.config.ts] import ui from '@nuxt/ui/vite' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ ui({ experimental: { componentDetection: true } }) ] }) ``` > [!NOTE] > Pass an array of component names instead to include components rendered with `` that can't be detected. ## :rocket: Features * ### Patch Changes

- 4d1b345: feat(provider/moonshotai): own the chat implementation, support video input. The provider no longer builds on `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`; the converter, language model, and helpers are owned by the package. Video file parts (e.g. `mediaType: 'video/mp4'`) are converted to Moonshot's `video_url` content parts for video-capable models (`kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.6`, `kimi-k2.5`). Audio and PDF file parts now throw client-side (the API rejects those part types). `reasoningHistory: 'preserved'` now maps to Moonshot's `thinking.keep: 'all'` request field (previously a no-op, the API ignores `reasoning_history`), gated per model with a warning on models without `thinking.keep` support. Adds `promptCacheKey` and `safetyIdentifier` provider options, widens `reasoningEffort` to `'low' | 'high' | 'max'` per Moonshot's docs, maps the generic `reasoning` call option to `reasoning_effort`, and passes `ms://` Files API references through natively (declared in `supportedUrls`).
